name: pdk-orchard-tenant-sync-redis-outages
instr:
We run three `src/OrchardCore.Cms.Web` processes against one PostgreSQL database and one Redis. Today a tenant created on one process can be absent on another; changes made while Redis is unavailable can disappear from other processes, and competing tenant requests can claim the same URL prefix. Make the Default tenant's management API cluster-safe without changing its existing single-process semantics.

A tenant created with `POST /api/tenants/create` and installed with `POST /api/tenants/setup` on one process serves its home page on all three within 10 seconds. Disabling it with `POST /api/tenants/disable/{name}` stops routing it on all three within 10 seconds. If Redis is unavailable for up to 30 seconds, successful disable and enable requests on different processes still take effect on every process within 30 seconds of recovery. A process started while Redis is down serves Default, recovers its Redis connection without restart, and applies later changes from other processes within 30 seconds of recovery. Concurrent creates of different tenant names with the same URL prefix produce one success and one 400, with that prefix routing to the winner on all three processes. Concurrent enable and disable requests for a running tenant result in exactly one successful transition; every process reflects that successful call within 10 seconds. Keep the existing create, setup, enable and disable routes and their single-instance responses: repeat disable of a disabled tenant returns 4
